name_reason: Already fully compliant: data_fd2_ prefix (game global), battle domain (battle core table), summon_anim_variant_a descriptor, 6slot is the real array dimension (matches int[6], a domain dimension not an address residue), frame_counter_array reflects the data type. No Ghidra address residue (no hex suffix matching 0x53fe4). Reflects both purpose and data type.
purpose: Runtime per-slot frame counter for the variant-A 6-slot summon-spell (召喚系) animation state machine.
logic_summary: Zero-init .bss scratch (24 bytes), populated by the INIT branch before any tick frame reads it (zero fill never observed at runtime). Sole accessor fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_a_6slot @ 0x269D3 (entry +0x10 / idx 4 of the 10-element summon-spell tick dispatch table at 0x523B9). INIT (state_code 0): frame[i] = -2*i, staggering each slot's start (0,-2,-4,-6,-8,-10). Tick states {2,5,8}: if 0 <= frame[i] < 7 blit the slot sprite; frame[i]++; if frame[i]==8 and terminate flag clear, reset frame[i]=0 (re-jitter color/jitter siblings). Loop bound is 6 slots.
element_semantics: Per-slot animation frame counter; signed int32, 4-byte stride, 6 elements. Range -2..7 during a slot cycle then wraps to 0. Negative values are the staggered-start phase before the slot becomes visible (blit gated on 0 <= frame < 7).
notes: datatype/element semantics and comment in src (btltab2.c lines 342-371) already match the disassembly evidence (MOV [EAX*4+0x53FE4]; signed JL/JGE bound tests vs 0 and 7; INC; loop bound CMP ...,0x6/JL). is_const=false confirmed: fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_a_6slot writes the array (INIT store, INC, reset to 0), so it has game-side writers (runtime .bss scratch in .object2). Ghidra plate was null (the description lived in a PRE_COMMENT); per the data-plate convention I wrote a concise PLATE_COMMENT (src-conclusion-based) and cleared the now-redundant PRE_COMMENT. Aside (not an issue for THIS symbol): in the INIT and frame==8 branches the consumer calls fd2_advance_rng_state() but discards its return; the jitter value is (i%2 ? 7 : 0) computed from the loop index, so the RNG call is a state-advance side effect only -- this concerns the jitter byte[6] sibling's documentation, not the frame_counter array, and is faithful in the decompiled C (no equivalence bug). src comment kept unchanged, so only the shard file is staged for this symbol (other pre-existing dirty shards in the worktree are from separate refiner runs and were deliberately not staged).
